t: Subsection (c) of section 844 of title 10, United States Code (article 44 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended to read as follows:“(c)(1) A court-martial with a military judge alone is a trial in the sense of this section (article) if, without fault of the accused—“(A) after introduction of evidence; and“(B) before announcement of findings under section 853 of this title (article 53);the case is dismissed or terminated by the convening authority or on motion of the prosecution for failure of available evidence or witnesses.“(2) A court-martial with a military judge and members is a trial in the sense of this section (article) if, without fault of the accused—“(A) after the members, having taken an oath as members under section 842 of this title (article 42) and after completion of challenges under section 841 of this title (article 41), are impaneled; and“(B) before announcement of findings under section 853 of this title (article 53);the case is dismissed or terminated by the convening authority or on motion of the prosecution for failure of available evidence or witnesses.”.

fable.w: This section amends the UCMJ's former-jeopardy article to define when a court-martial counts as a trial (when jeopardy attaches). The tempting reading is that references to court-martial 'members', 'challenges', or a 'motion of the prosecution' suggest outside involvement, but these are all military justice actors and procedures inside the federal government. It concerns individual criminal adjudication, not consultation with outsiders on a federal decision, and it creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: A court-martial with a military judge alone is a trial in the sense of this section (article) if, without fault of the accused

qwen_block.w: This section defines when a military proceeding constitutes a 'trial' for the purposes of the Uniform Code of Military Justice. It involves internal military justice procedures between the convening authority, the prosecution, the military judge, and the accused service member. There is no requirement for consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government (such as the general public, states, or non-federal entities) before a decision is made. The actors involved are all part of the federal military justice system.
qwen_block.s: A court-martial with a military judge alone is a trial in the sense of this section (article) if, without fault of the accused—(A) after introduction of evidence; and (B) before announcement of findings under section 853 of this title (article 53); the case is dismissed or terminated by the convening authority or on motion of the prosecution for failure of available evidence or witnesses.

opus.w: This provision defines when a court-martial counts as a 'trial' for double-jeopardy purposes under Article 44 of the UCMJ. Everyone involved (military judge, members, convening authority, prosecution) is inside the federal government, and no outside party is consulted or given a right to challenge a federal policy decision. Procedural words like 'members,' 'challenges,' and 'motion' describe how a military trial is run, not public participation.
opus.s: the case is dismissed or terminated by the convening authority or on motion of the prosecution for failure of available evidence or witnesses.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** It's tempting to read this as participation because it mentions court-martial "members," "challenges," and a "motion of the prosecution," which sound procedural. That reading fails. Everyone involved is military personnel (judge, members, convening authority, prosecution) acting inside the federal government. The section only defines when a court-martial counts as a "trial" for double-jeopardy purposes. No outside party is consulted before a federal decision, and no one gets a new right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines procedural conditions for what constitutes a 'trial' in the context of military justice, specifically regarding dismissals or terminations. It does not establish a process for outside parties to consult with or participate in federal decision-making. The actors involved (convening authority, prosecution, military judge) are all part of the federal government/military structure.
qwen_chat.s: A court-martial with a military judge alone is a trial in the sense of this section (article) if, without fault of the accused—(A) after introduction of evidence; and (B) before announcement of findings under section 853 of this title (article 53); the case is dismissed or terminated by the convening authority or on motion of the prosecution for failure of available evidence or witnesses.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "accused" (a service member) is an outside party participating in the decision to dismiss or terminate the case. However, the text describes procedural conditions for defining a "trial" for legal purposes (likely regarding double jeopardy or compensation), not a mechanism for the accused to consult with or influence the government's decision-making process. The dismissal is done by the convening authority or prosecution, not through a participatory process with the accused. Furthermore, military justice proceedings are internal administrative/judicial processes within the federal government structure.
